en.title: Longest Lexicographically Smallest Regular Expression
en.description:
A regular expression consists of uppercase letters and bracketed character classes; letters within a class must not repeat, and one class matches one character. Given x, y and z of equal length, find the longest regular expression that matches x and y but not z; among equal lengths take the lexicographically smallest. If there is no solution, output −1.

The standard input format, examples and test data were written independently by CSWork.
en.input: Three lines x, y and z, containing only uppercase English letters, each of length n (1..1000000). Lexicographic order follows ASCII character order.
en.output: Output the regular expression string, or −1.
en.explanation: Example 1: at the second position z=D is also the character of y, so it cannot be removed; at the first position C is removed, and all other letters of both character classes are kept, so the expression still matches AB and BD but not CD. Example 2: z equals x, so any expression matching x also matches z; there is no solution. Example 3: B could be removed at any position; to make the result lexicographically smallest, remove B only in the rightmost character class.
hints: Find the rightmost position where z[i] differs from both x[i] and y[i]. Output the full 26-letter class at every position, and remove z[i] only at the chosen position.
